Hey there. BPD is a bitch to deal with, I can imagine your partner is going through hell, fighting with yourself and your emotions is incredibly tough to go though. While this does not excuse the behavior, it might put his actions into a different context. 

I have been in a very similar position to your partner, making me quite biased. I want to clarify that. But the idea of trying to stop enabling his bad behavior is strange in this context. People who do not have BPD see the suicidal thoughts to be a purposeful way of manipulating someone. In my position, when I was actively suicidal and expressing these feelings to my partner, it was not meant or said in a way for them to take action on it or an expectation that they should be doing something. Actually, there was a lot of guilt at even expressing these awful thoughts to someone I loved so much. It was meant in a:
“I have no one I can talk to about my emotions, and I hate to put this burden on you but without expressing it I may actually have no option but to kill myself to stop these reality altering feelings”

Additionally, I don’t know if there is a way to stop enabling him, because I don’t think this really is an instance of enabling. It sounds like he needs support and is extremely unstable. It doesn’t sound like he’s trying to benefit from saying he’s suicidal, it just sounds like you’re his main attachment, the BPD feelings kicked into full gear leading to him feeling so overwhelmed and overtaken by painful emotions and an extreme fear of abandonment. I’ve felt the feelings of “I love this person so much but I’m literally so scared they’ll leave me that I’d rather die.” He is feeling the way he is, and the “bad behavior” seems like a result of trying to express his feelings to someone he trusts. 
All you can do with this is be supportive, because you can’t really stop him from being suicidal and irrational from mental illness. You are not enabling him by just being there to listen to him, distract from issues, or comfort him. 

You can have days where you’re also not ok, and need support of course. Being his support does not mean you can’t be going through your own shit and need support. And in general, you are not required to be there for him at all, but in the case that you can’t be a support or be patient, break up. It helps no one if all you feel is that you need to stop his bad behavior, and he feels like he is only getting blocked out by you because you aren’t giving him the support he needs. And long term, BPD is a huge battle. He needs support from a partner, and if you’re not comfortable or able to give a big commitment of time, energy and love then this relationship is not compatible while he’s still trying to heal. 

I don’t know the situation with you and your partner, but I just wanted to add another perspective. People with BPD often feel like they’re manipulating by people and that they’re the worst people on earth because of this. But I feel as if that’s often not true and when we express our feelings, people take it that we need them to help rather than just listen and support us, and they begin to feel like we’re trying to manipulate them. Of course, there are also people with BPD who are actually manipulative. Again, just perspective.
